proposals: The Central Electricity Authority should publish the state-wise and substation-level assumptions behind the Ministry of Power's 13.56 GW data-centre demand projection for FY2031–32, so that the one forecast built into transmission planning can be checked against where projects are actually being sited.

State transmission utilities in Maharashtra and the National Capital Region should publish available load headroom at the substations serving data-centre clusters, updated quarterly, so that developers and regulators can see the transmission bottleneck this post identifies before campuses are committed.

MeitY should maintain a public register of data-centre capacity by state, separating commissioned IT load in MW from announced commitments, so that company figures such as the more than $210 billion from Adani and Reliance can be tracked as built capacity rather than headline pledges.

TRAI should publish, for each cable landing station, lit capacity in commercial use alongside design capacity, so that the Chennai, Mumbai and Tuticorin figures used to explain data-centre location reflect usable bandwidth rather than theoretical maxima.

State water resources departments in data-centre states should require large facilities to report annual cooling-water consumption and source, so that the roughly 780 million litres a year a single 30 MW facility can use is measured across the actual fleet in water-stressed locations.
